At a proper source fiber, the full affine cap margin takes both strict signs and the section has positive coarea. The two-source quota then requires a positive outside coarea beyond the slab. The one-sided premise places it on the left. Interpolation from an earlier support plane point to a strictly captured point at a excludes a second outside support on that side. Reflection and reversal of the continuous margin give the other geometric cases. The projection endpoint assertion follows by applying the same interpolation to any proposed earlier point of the closed cut body.

All intermediate fibers between L and b have positive volume by interpolation of positive endpoint fibers. A plane point at L and strictly captured point at b give a captured point at every intermediate base, while strictly missed endpoint points give the other sign. Thus all integer fibers L+1 through b are proper.

The full supporting section at L and any plane point at b give a translated (b−z)/h dilation in the section at z, since the ambient affine plane is preserved by convex combinations. All sections have the same continuous normal divisor. The section contribution and the dropped nonnegative inside term produce exactly m∑_{j=1}^{h−1}(j/h)^{d−1}≤h−m.

For d≥2 and h≥m+1≥2 the increasing right-endpoint Riemann sum gives the first strict inequality, and strict Bernoulli gives (1−1/h)^d>1−d/h. If m≥d this makes the lower bound exceed h−m. For d=1, counting coarea 1/‖u‖ on the h proper sections gives mh≤h−m, impossible for m≥1.
